local_articles.title: The Open 2026: Tee times, TV details, weather forecast, players to watch
local_articles.snippet: When and where is it on? The final men’s Major of the year, the Open Championship will begin at Royal Birkdale early on Thursday morning. It is the 154th edition of golf’s oldest Major and the 11th time it has been hosted at the Southport course. The tournament will run until Sunday afternoon, where the winner will be presented with the Claret Jug. How can I follow the tournament? You can watch some 15 hours of live coverage on Sky Sports from 6.30am to 9.30pm. On Saturday and Sunday, coverage starts from 8am. Keep an eye out though should England beat Argentina to make the World Cup final, as the R&A have said they could move Sunday’s tee times to earlier in the day should that come to pass. local_articles.title: Scheffler eyes rare Open repeat as Royal Birkdale bakes in summer heat
local_articles.snippet: LONDON, July 13 - American Scottie Scheffler will set out to buck a British Open trend and become the first player to defend the title for 18 years at a baked Royal Birkdale this week. Ireland's Padraig Harrington was the last player to retain the Claret Jug when he won at Birkdale in 2008 and the trend since then has favoured first-time winners. South African Ernie Els was the most recent repeat champion, at Royal Lytham & St Annes in 2012, since when the sport's oldest major has been a hot potato. Several players will be favoured to snap the sequence of first-time winners, though, with world number one Scheffler and Northern Ireland's Rory McIlroy the favourites despite both coming in with question marks about their form. Scheffler produced a links golf masterclass on the Antrim coast last year with a processional four-stroke victory at Portrush adding a fourth major to his collection.

local_articles.title: Hometown hero Tommy Fleetwood chasing his Major dream at Royal Birkdale
local_articles.snippet: us golfing son is still waiting to see the tide in his own affairs. Tommy Fleetwood is arguably the best golfer on the planet yet to win a Major championship, so the prospect of ending his drought at Royal Birkdale this week is the plotline that will prove most irresistible to the galleries. Fleetwood is the hometown hero and his face is daubed all over Liverpool. There’s a 50-metre mural of him splashed on the wall of the Southport and Birkdale Sports Club less than a mile from Royal Birkdale, while a 1,000-square-metre portrait of his face has been installed outside the Liverpool One shopping centre. Fleetwood first started swinging a golf club at Southport Municipal and became a member at Formby Hall. local_articles.title: Apple’s ‘Thermonuclear’ Response to the OpenAI Threat
local_articles.snippet: Steve Jobs declared “thermonuclear war” on Google’s Android operating system in 2010, calling it a “stolen product.” Now, his successor is going to battle against Apple’s new most dangerous rival. In one of his last acts as Apple’s chief executive before successor John Ternus takes over, Tim Cook fired a missile at OpenAI. In a lawsuit filed Friday, Apple alleged that a senior OpenAI executive, who once sat atop Apple’s own product design team, was involved in a monthslong campaign to steal Apple trade secrets. Although it isn’t yet clear what evidence the company has to back up all its claims, the suit lands before OpenAI has released a product and as the technology industry races to build artificial-intelligence-powered devices that can move society beyond the smartphone era. The winner could dominate the future just as Apple’s iPhone has ruled the consumer market for the last 20 years

local_articles.title: Chelsea's new boss Alonso demands hunger and passion ahead of Premier League campaign
local_articles.snippet: July 13 - Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso said he wants to see greater hunger and a desire to improve from his players as he prepares for his first Premier League season in charge. Chelsea finished tenth in the league last season following a disappointing, trophyless campaign and failed to qualify for European competition. "We need hunger, passion, we need to want to improve," Alonso told reporters on Monday. "The Premier League is so competitive. We need to prepare ourselves, we need to be determined in the details, in how we want to play. But the most important bit is our game." SQUAD CHANGES Alonso also addressed the future of winger Alejandro Garnacho, who has been linked with a move away from Stamford Bridge as the club look to reshape their squad. local_articles.title: United sign Brazil midfielder Santos from Chelsea
local_articles.snippet: July 13 - Manchester United have signed Brazil midfielder Andrey Santos from fellow Premier League side Chelsea on a deal until June 2031, both clubs said on Monday. United have reportedly paid an initial fee of 48 million pounds ($64.30 million) for Santos, with a further two million pounds potentially payable in add-ons. "To be honest, since when I was young, I dreamed of this moment. The history, the responsibility that comes with this badge, that's why I'm here," Santos, 22, said in a video shared by United on social media. Santos joined Chelsea in 2023 and had loan spells at Brazilian Serie A side Vasco da Gama, Nottingham Forest and Strasbourg before returning to Stamford Bridge for the 2025-26 campaign. questions.title: Who will hold the men's outdoor mile world record immediately after the 2026 London Diamond League meeting?

questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : World Athletics reports or reputable contemporaneous news coverage of the London Diamond League meeting on July 18, 2026. Resolution : Resolve to the athlete credited as the men's outdoor mile world-record holder at the conclusion of the meeting. If no new world record is set, resolve to the existing record holder. Later administrative ratification is not required if the performance is reported as a world record. Accepted Answer Format : The athlete's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Three major developments by July 10 sharply narrow the field ahead of the July 18 London Diamond League Emsley Carr Mile: (1) Irish Times (July 4) confirmed Jakob Ingebrigtsen has yet to race at all in 2026 while recovering from early-February Achilles tendon surgery, eliminating his prior 9% probability with just 8 days left; (2) the July 4 Prefontaine Classic Bowerman Mile (won by 20-year-old Australian Cameron Myers in 3:46.06 NR ahead of Yared Nuguse in 3:46.61) and July 10 Monaco Diamond League (no mile race; Emmanuel Wanyonyi broke the 1,000m WR) passed without a mile WR, leaving London as essentially the sole remaining opportunity; (3) Marathon Handbook/CITIUS Mag (July 7) confirmed Yared Nuguse (3:43.97 PB, #4 all-time, 0.84s off WR) entered the London mile to crash Josh Kerr's 'Project 222' attempt (custom Brooks spikes, speed suit, hand-picked pacers, strong WR-pace intervals, 3:45.34 PB). Removing Ingebrigtsen boosts reigning 27-year record holder Hicham El Guerrouj (3:43.13) from 0.76 -> 0.83, doubles Nuguse 0.03 -> 0.06, holds Kerr at 0.07, adds red-hot Cameron Myers (3:28.00 1500m & 3:46.06 mile) at 0.02, and keeps Niels Laros at 0.01 (1% residual).

questions.title: Who will be appointed head of Syria’s National Security Bureau in July 2026?
questions.background: The National Security Bureau oversees Syria’s security agencies.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official Syrian government announcement or reporting by the Syrian state news agency SANA identifying the person appointed head of the National Security Bureau during July 2026. Resolution Date : The date the appointment is publicly announced. Accepted Answer Format : The appointee’s full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Syria's Ba'athist National Security Bureau was dissolved after Bashar al-Assad's fall, and President Ahmed al-Sharaa established a National Security Council in March 2025 alongside a restructured General Intelligence Service (initially led by Anas Khattab, who became Interior Minister in spring 2025, and since May 2025 by Hussein al-Salama). If Damascus establishes or revives a National Security Bureau in July 2026 to coordinate security agencies, sitting General Intelligence chief Hussein al-Salama and Interior Minister/former spy chief Anas Khattab (al-Sharaa's top security architect) are the leading internal candidates, followed by Defense Minister Murhaf Abu Qasra, Chief of General Staff Ali Noureddine al-Naasan, and senior presidential/interior insider Ali Keda. Given Damascus's history of elevating lesser-known former HTS security commanders whose full names emerge only upon SANA announcement, a full 50% tail mass is left outside these five figures.

local_articles.title: Leaving Al Hol: A Syrian father on survival, freedom and what comes next
local_articles.snippet: Until the start of this year, Fade (28), his wife and four children lived in Al Hol. The notorious detention camp in northeast Syria held tens of thousands of people accused of having links to Islamic State (also known as Isis). The detainees did not undergo any formal legal process. Human rights organisations condemned their detention as arbitrary and illegal under international law. In February, in a shock change of fortunes, the camp was closed after Syria’s new government took control of the area, ousting the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF). Fade asked to be identified by his first name only, saying he did not want to be associated with that experience for the rest of his life. local_articles.title: ‘It’s expensive’: Syria’s electricity has improved, but challenges remain
local_articles.snippet: Damascus, Syria – Nasri Tadros sweeps dust away from the electric scooters parked outside his small shop in central Damascus. “I have three generators for my shop, and this runs on batteries,” he said, pointing to a battery-operated lighter he uses to fire up charcoal. He stepped into the narrow shop that he rents, where he has worked for the past two years, selling and delivering products for hookahs. Around Damascus, solar panels and diesel generators are a common sight. During the harshest years of the war, they supplemented the sparse state-provided electricity, which only came a few hours a day between long cuts. As Damascus enters the summer months, there is concern about the dry heat, which reaches the high 30s in Celsius (up to almost 100F). questions.title: Which driver will rank second in the Formula One drivers' championship immediately after the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix?
questions.background: The drivers' championship standings reflect cumulative points earned during the season, with ties resolved under Formula One's championship rules.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The post-race drivers' championship standings published by the FIA or Formula One. Resolution : Resolve to the driver ranked second in the championship standings following the Belgian Grand Prix scheduled for July 19, 2026, before any subsequent race takes place. Accepted Answer Format : The driver's name.
questions.current_reasoning: Post-Silverstone British GP (July 5, Reuters/FIA) turns the post-Spa P2 standings race into a pure two-driver contest with a significant structural advantage for George Russell. Charles Leclerc won behind the safety car while Russell stayed out to finish P2 (+18) ahead of Lewis Hamilton in P3 (+15, stewards took no further action on his yellow-flag investigation after Ferrari's late pitstop dropped him behind Russell), and Kimi Antonelli scored 0 (P16 after a front-left wheel shield kerb failure and 5s track limits penalty). With only ONE non-sprint race left before resolution (Belgian GP, July 19, max 25 pts, no fastest-lap point), standings are: Antonelli 179 (5 wins), Russell 154 (2 wins), Hamilton 147 (1 win), Leclerc 108 (1 win). Antonelli is mathematically guaranteed P1 (even a Russell win + Antonelli 0 ties at 179, which Antonelli wins 5-3 on win countback), and Leclerc (max 133) is mathematically eliminated—removing Antonelli's 0.005 tail completely. Russell expanded his lead over Hamilton from +4 to +7 pts AND holds the win-countback tiebreak (2 vs 1), meaning Hamilton must outscore Russell by >=8 pts at Spa (or win Spa while Russell finishes P2 and win P2-finish countback, where Russell already holds multiple P2s including Spain and Silverstone). Monte Carlo Spa simulations blending Mercedes's power-circuit edge (9/9 poles in 2026) with Ferrari's strong high-speed Silverstone form (2 wins in last 3 races) and ~9-10% DNF/rain chaos place Russell at 68-73% (baseline 0.70, up from 0.63) and Hamilton at 0.30 (down from 0.365).
